video_title: Head Coach Jordan Ott Practice Media Availability | 10-19-26

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott provides update on player's injury recovery status
quotes.excerpt: He did more today for sure, hard practice. This was the test day to see exactly where he's at.
quotes.quote: He did more today for sure, hard practice. This was the test day to see exactly where he's at. Tomorrow will be a lower day, trying to be right for Wednesday.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says a key player went through a hard practice today as a test for his injury recovery. The team is monitoring him closely to see if he is ready for Wednesday.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott discusses the team's competitive depth and roster competition
quotes.excerpt: A lot of good players competing for spots. We've got a deep team, so we really like our depth.
quotes.quote: It's exactly what we said before the camp, a competitive camp. A lot of good players competing for spots. We've got a deep team, so we really like our depth, because that gets tested throughout the 82-game season, so in a good spot.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott is happy with the team depth heading into the season. He says it is a competitive camp with a lot of players fighting for spots.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on center rotation strategy and player development
quotes.excerpt: Whoever starts, got to play well, whoever comes off the bench got to play well.
quotes.quote: Two guys that we love. We got, we need 48 minutes, great center play. You've seen both of their growth from different pieces, and we'll keep trying to figure it out as we get close to Wednesday, but we're in a good spot again with our center spot. We got to play 48 minutes, whoever starts, got to play well, whoever comes off the bench got to play well. Doesn't mean who starts or ends the game. We need 48 minutes of great center play.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on the center rotation. He says they need 48 minutes of great play from the position regardless of who starts or finishes the game.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on game-to-game adjustments and team performance focus
quotes.excerpt: We're not going into the game worried about the opponent as much, we got to play well ourselves.
quotes.quote: I'm not one to change kind of game to game. Again, we need 48 minutes. You're trying to put it together for 48 minutes. If someone gets in foul trouble or someone's struggling with a matchup early, then you adjust, but we're not going into the game worried about the opponent as much, we got to play well ourselves. So each night when you go into the game, you play well and then we'll read the game as we go.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says he prefers not to change his approach game to game. He wants the team to focus on playing well themselves rather than worrying too much about the opponent.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on Mark's veteran presence and defensive versatility
quotes.excerpt: Mark brings size, skill. He's been in those situations, he's a little bit more veteran in some of those situations.
quotes.quote: I got to think that's a big piece of what Mark brings. Mark brings size, skill. He's been in those situations, he's a little bit more veteran in some of those situations. But there's a lot of things that Mark also brings. Ability to switch, ability to force turnovers late in the game, ability to pass, to think out there and help us. So it's going to again, that'll change game to game and some of it we do have to see. We got to see exactly what we're going to do end of the game with that spot.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott highlights the versatility of Mark. He notes that Mark brings size and skill and is a key piece for late game defensive situations.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on managing opening night jitters and team challenges
quotes.excerpt: Lillard's return in Portland is something that I'm sure we'll feel, but that quickly wears off.
quotes.quote: Everyone has a different feeling going into opening night. Like the energy will be different. Lillard's return in Portland is something that I'm sure we'll feel, but that quickly wears off. Like after a couple minutes, it's just back to playing. So there'll be some challenges that this group has not faced. That's really what you try to figure out early in the game. How are we going to play together, how are we going to overcome the first point of adversity, can we gather ourselves and not let an opponent get on a large run?
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on opening night jitters. He expects the energy to be different but says the focus for the group is on how they handle early adversity.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on spatial awareness and team offensive evolution
quotes.excerpt: That's how the game is evolving. It's a lot of concepts, it's a lot of spatial awareness.
quotes.quote: That's how the game is evolving. It's a lot of concepts, it's a lot of spatial awareness. It's a lot of reading your teammate, does he have an advantage, does he not, and then getting to your superpowers. We've had that since day one, and we're developing it. And especially a team like Portland that plays so aggressive on the basketball, a lot of times your five is your outlet, similar to how we kind of saw San Antonio the first game we played.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says the game is evolving toward concepts and spatial awareness. He notes that against aggressive teams, the five man often acts as an outlet.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on team selflessness and floor spacing
quotes.excerpt: It's the selflessness to run, thinking you can get the ball but you may not.
quotes.quote: I think it's the selflessness first off to run without it. Get your head up. We have especially with so many impactful wings or guards that can bring it themselves, that helps. But it's the selflessness to run, thinking you can get the ball but you may not. Even if you don't get the ball, it leads you to stretch the floor. And then it always comes back to Book skips it. Book will get it, wake up the floor, he'll skip it. That encourages and highlights it for everyone.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott praises the selflessness of his team. He notes that even when players do not get the ball, their movement helps stretch the floor for others.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on offensive consistency and decision-making
quotes.excerpt: It's not just the shooting piece, it's the decision-making piece, it's the spacing piece that goes along with it.
quotes.quote: It's a constant process. I think it's not just the shooting piece, it's the decision-making piece, it's the spacing piece that goes along with it. Then it's also the belief even if it does come off the rim, we'll go get it. So it's a kind of all of it. And then you have players in and out during the season, your offense is going to look a little bit different based on the personnel that you have.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says offensive consistency is a constant process involving shooting, decision making, and spacing.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on coaching staff evolution and continuous improvement
quotes.excerpt: We've gotten better as a coaching staff. Hopefully everyone in the building has gotten better.
quotes.quote: It's never about us as coaches. It's like we all have to get better. I think it's a challenge for all of us. Players, we've asked them to get better in the summer. We've gotten better as a coaching staff. Hopefully everyone in the building has gotten better. That you got to evolve. This game moves so fast. I think you see it even in the preseason, some playoff solutions or successes are now getting translated to early offense or early defensive concepts.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says the coaching staff must continue to evolve because the game moves so fast.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on team culture and player leadership
quotes.excerpt: He just brings a joy. It's similar to Man-Man just in a different kind of way.
quotes.quote: It's him. I think it's him. I think the reputation that he's built as an incredible teammate, a great in the locker room. Obviously I know multiple of his former coaches. They all say the same thing and it starts with the spirit that he has every day. He just brings a joy. It's similar to Man-Man just in a different kind of way. He's just great to be around. So great to be around, it's easier to engage. He's a accomplished a lot in his career, he's a established veteran player that I think everyone respects.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott praises a veteran player for his leadership and spirit, calling him an incredible teammate who is great to be around.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on maintaining team standards throughout the season
quotes.excerpt: It's always about getting the right guys that enjoy doing something a little bit different.
quotes.quote: It's always about getting the right guys that enjoy doing something a little bit different. And then now can we maintain it? Again, it's easy to talk about in the preseason, but when you're tired, when those possessions become a little bit more tough, can we continue to do those those little micro margins and windows and edges? Goodies are ring leader of a lot of that stuff, just his energy and he's just again, joy to just go out and play and compete that makes it easier for other guys to follow him.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott says the challenge for the team is maintaining their standards throughout the long season when things get tough.

quotes.speaker: Jordan Ott
quotes.summary_phrase: Jordan Ott on assessing his own development as a head coach
quotes.excerpt: We have to continually get better and prove yourself. That's why it's the most competitive basketball league.
quotes.quote: We'll see. I think a little bit is we'll see, you know, you got to prove it again. I don't think the players, coaches, staff, this league doesn't really matter what you did last year. We have to continually get better and prove yourself. That's why it's the most competitive basketball league in the world. Everyone's trying to get better, trying to grow, trying to get your spot. We had 45 wins last year, but we have zero right now. And we're going to have to find ways to win game one.
quotes.social_post: Jordan Ott on the upcoming season. He says that despite winning 45 games last year, the team starts at zero and has to prove itself all over again.
